run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. Please
investigate the root cause using the app-260-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The log evidence in `app-260-prod-logs` is for the cluster the question names: 8 of the index's 10 documents in the authorized window carry `cluster=production-us-east-2` (the other 2 carry `cluster=production-eu-west-2`). In production-us-east-2 the failure chain is consistent: payment-service's calls to the external payment provider `stripe-us` time out (`Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms`, status 504, at 03:47:31 and 05:02:31) and checkout-service returns 500 to `POST /api/checkout` naming the same provider (`payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)` at 03:47:31 on the same correlation_id `chk-us-2142`, `payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway` at 05:17:31, and `circuit-breaker open for payment-service` at 04:47:31 and 05:42:31). payment-service itself recorded `Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031` at 05:32:31. So the deepest evidenced cause is the external upstream `stripe-us`, with payment-service and checkout-service as consecutive victims. This is stated as partial, not supported, because the external provider's own state is only visible through our log lines and a status-page reference, and because Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for this run and my Kubernetes access covers only production-eu-west-2, so no us-east-2 pod, metric or trace corroboration exists here. The production-eu-west-2 side was checked and showed no matching failure (successful card payments in its checkout pod logs through 05:46:55, `Stripe-EU responding normally`).

claims.text: In the authorized window `app-260-prod-logs` holds 10 documents (02:47:31Z to 05:42:31Z) aggregated as cluster=production-us-east-2 (8) and cluster=production-eu-west-2 (2), service=checkout-service (6) and service=payment-service (4), level ERROR (6), WARN (2), INFO (2), status_code 500 (4), 200 (4), 504 (2). The index maps fields cluster, region, correlation_id, level, message, service, status_code, timestamp.

production-us-east-2 payment-service logged ERROR status 504 `Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms` twice: 2026-11-21T03:47:31Z (correlation_id chk-us-2142) and 2026-11-21T05:02:31Z (correlation_id chk-us-2220).

production-us-east-2 checkout-service logged ERROR status 500 on `POST /api/checkout` at 2026-11-21T03:47:31Z `payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)` with correlation_id chk-us-2142 — the same correlation_id as payment-service's 504 at that same timestamp — and at 05:17:31Z `payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway` (correlation_id chk-us-2252).

production-us-east-2 checkout-service logged ERROR status 500 `circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)` at 2026-11-21T04:47:31Z (correlation_id chk-us-2208) and `circuit-breaker open for payment-service` at 2026-11-21T05:42:31Z (correlation_id chk-us-2280).
production-us-east-2 payment-service logged WARN status 200 at 2026-11-21T05:32:31Z: `Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031`.

The earliest document in the index for production-us-east-2 is a checkout-service WARN at 2026-11-21T02:47:31Z: `Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1700ms (target 800ms)` (correlation_id chk-us-2001) — the only latency statement available for this cluster inside the window.

The two production-eu-west-2 documents in the same index are healthy-path statements from a different cluster: checkout-service INFO `Healthy: p95 latency 230ms over last 5 minutes` at 2026-11-21T03:47:31Z and payment-service INFO `Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms` at 2026-11-21T04:47:31Z.

In the cluster I can read (the Kubernetes context holding namespaces app-100a, otel-demo, kube-system), the `checkout` deployment in namespace otel-demo reports 1 ready / 1 available replica and the `payment` deployment likewise; pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logs from 03:47:42Z to 05:46:55Z contain repeated INFO `payment went through (transaction_id: ...)` lines and no error, failure or timeout line for payment calls, and pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d produced only one `MetadataLookupWarning` line in that period. This is production-eu-west-2 data per my access, not evidence about production-us-east-2.

Fault injection through the demo feature-flag set was considered as the cause of the payment failures: ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo defines `paymentFailure` (Fail payment service charge requests n%) and `paymentUnreachable` (Payment service is unavailable), and both have `defaultVariant` `off` with state ENABLED, i.e. not switched on; that ConfigMap also belongs to the production-eu-west-2 cluster I can read, not to production-us-east-2. Rejected as the cause of the us-east-2 failures.

A rollout or pod replacement of checkout/payment as the trigger was considered: no pod events for namespace otel-demo appear among the window's events (grouped events exist only for Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod/Endpoints in namespace app-100a), the checkout and payment pods were created 2026-11-20T16:32:07Z and kept their names, and their controllers' ReplicaSets are unchanged; the pods show a container restart with `lastState.terminated` exitCode 255, reason `Unknown`, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, restartCount 1. That in-place container restart is not a rollout and, in the eu-west-2 cluster, is not tied by any evidence to the us-east-2 payment failures.

Primary hypothesis: the external payment provider `stripe-us` is the origin of the incident in production-us-east-2 — the provider's charge endpoint timed out at 30s and is in a self-declared degraded mode, so payment-service's 504s and checkout-service's 500s and open circuit breaker are downstream consequences. Supporting facts are the two 504 `Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms` lines, the checkout line naming `provider=stripe-us` on the shared correlation_id chk-us-2142, and `Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031`.

Secondary hypothesis (amplifier, not independent cause): checkout-service's breaker setting `failure rate 41% > 25% threshold` makes it fail fast with 500 once payment-service passes a 25% failure rate, which is why 500s continued at 04:47:31 and 05:42:31 while the provider 504s were logged at 03:47:31 and 05:02:31; no evidence shows the threshold itself was changed during the window, so its contribution to severity is unquantified.

Treat this as an external-dependency incident: obtain the provider's (stripe-us) status-page incident record and confirm whether the 30s charge timeout and the 502 responses are on their side; until then avoid raising retry volume against a queue that already reported depth 1031.

Once Prometheus/Jaeger and production-us-east-2 cluster access are available, corroborate with checkout-service and payment-service error-rate and latency series (`traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,status_code}`, `rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count{rpc_service,rpc_method,rpc_grpc_status_code}`) over 02:47–05:47Z and read the us-east-2 pods' own status, events and logs, since none of that could be observed in this run.

gaps: No metrics or traces could be read: `execute_prometheus_instant_query`, `metrics_range_query`, `get_all_labels`, `traces_search` and `traces_list_services` all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for target m0-otel-20260909, so no error rate, request count or latency series for checkout/payment in production-us-east-2 is known; absence of such series is unknown, not zero.

My Kubernetes access is only the cluster containing namespaces app-100a/otel-demo/kube-system (production-eu-west-2 per my access); no pods, deployments, services, endpoints, networkpolicies, resourcequotas or events for production-us-east-2 could be read, so the us-east-2 workloads' own status and application logs are unchecked.

The external provider `stripe-us` is outside every available source; its state is known only from our own log lines (`Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms`, `Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031`) and could not be verified directly.

Change history is not an integrated source in this run, so whether a configuration, secret or provider credential changed before 02:47:31Z is unknown; secrets are unreadable, so any credential-related cause could not be verified.

Only 10 log documents exist in the index (earliest 2026-11-21T02:47:31Z), so there is no same-cluster baseline before the 02:47:31Z p95=1700ms WARN; the eu-west-2 lines (p95 230ms, Stripe-EU 180ms) are a different cluster and are not treated as that baseline.

In the production-eu-west-2 cluster, the checkout and payment containers show `lastState.terminated` exitCode 255 reason `Unknown` at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z (restartCount 1, pods unchanged, no owning-object events for otel-demo); nothing observed explains this restart and it cannot be placed as impact or as a change for another reason.
Customer-facing impact beyond the logged `POST /api/checkout failed` 500s (e.g. frontend error rates, abandoned carts, revenue loss) was not observed in any available source.
next_steps: Pull stripe-us's own incident timeline/status page for 2026-11-21T02:47Z–05:47Z and correlate with the observed 30s `/v1/charges` timeouts and the 502 responses.

When Prometheus is reachable, compare checkout-service and payment-service `http_server_request_duration_seconds_count` / `traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code}` before and after 02:47:31Z to quantify the error-rate step and check whether any other service in production-us-east-2 deviated.
Obtain read access to the production-us-east-2 cluster and inspect the checkout/payment pods' status, container last termination reasons, events and application logs for the same window.

Confirm whether the checkout circuit-breaker threshold (25% failure rate) and payment-service retry/timeout settings were changed before the incident, via the change-history integration that is not available in this run.
